text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and tool outputs, and the cautious 'inconclusive' leaning plus targeted-chart next step is reasonable. But the summary has substantive weaknesses: the headline omits the strong billing-level signal, the closing line is contradictory, and the example claims are thin. An investigator would need to redo some analysis.","problems":["Headline reports only chart usability (18 of 30 usable, 1 below billed) and omits the main finding: 99215 at 8.9x expected, z=2.98.","'no upcoding shown in the charts received' is poorly supported: only 3 documented 99215 claims, and it sits oddly next to the strong statistical outlier signal; it could be read as exculpatory.","Rationale says 'against 14% for the comparison providers' but the 1 of 3 below-billed rate is not meaningfully comparable given n=3; no caveat about the tiny n beyond 'weak sample'.","Examples cite C0108806 and C0108807 as low-complexity 99215s, but C0108807 has a dx of R10.9 (abdominal pain) that is not discussed. The two supported claims (C0108832, C0108911, documented high MDM with 54 and 48 minutes) were not cited, so counter-evidence is missing.","The cited claims were not requested from the practice; next steps do not say that C0108805 is the only documented below-billed claim, nor address the deficiencies (missing signature, missing visits, missing results) or follow up on the 12 missing charts.","Does not state the 'no 99215 claims on high-complexity patients' fact or the by-complexity share pattern (e.g. 31% 99215 among 2-condition patients vs 5.9% for all providers), which would explain the billed level vs patient complexity.","Note-signal statistics (problems 33%, late 11%, data 11%) are listed without interpretation; 'No audit trail was received' is not tied to a next step."]}
